page.name: Order confirmations
page.h1: Send order confirmations customers can keep
page.metaTitle: Order confirmations over your own accounts
page.metaDescription: Order confirmations with the reference, the total and the next step — sent immediately, never throttled away, and logged for support.
page.lede: The confirmation is the message your customer keeps — forwarded, screenshotted, quoted back to support. Send it the moment the order lands, on a channel they actually read, and let the log answer for it later.

sections.h: What a customer needs to see
bullets: The order reference, prominently — it is what support will ask for
What was bought, at least in summary
A link to the order in your own system

sections.h: Send it the moment the order lands
p: Confirmation is transactional and should not queue behind promotional traffic. Keeping the two message types distinct means a large campaign does not delay the message that tells someone their payment worked.
bullets: Transactional sends are not filtered by opt-out suppression
Each send is logged with its status, so support can answer from the record
Delivery receipts are recorded wherever the provider reports delivery back

sections.h: Same event, whichever channel they read
p: Whether a confirmation goes out on SMS, email, WhatsApp, or more than one of them, is a decision about the customer rather than about the technology. The platform connects the accounts you hold on each channel and sends on the ones you choose.

faq.q: Should the confirmation be in the same channel as the checkout?
faq.a: Not necessarily — it is whichever channel the customer will actually look at. Multiple channels can be connected and chosen per send.

faq.q: Can we include a discount code?
faq.a: Content is yours to compose; the platform sends what it is given. Treat a discount in a transactional message as a marketing decision with its own consent implications.
The send records its error, and the failure is visible in the logs. A retry is a decision your system makes, remembering that a retry sends a second message.
